clue.text: Class project has point

parts.note: to project an image is to cast it
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A school project on social class has a sharp point to make.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social rank, so it is a class in the social sense.

clue.text: Curvaceous leg and bottom of skirt visible in carriage

parts.note: a cabriole is a curved furniture leg, as on Queen Anne chairs

indicators.note: bottom of in a down clue means the final letter of skirt

explanation.surface: A shapely leg and the hem of a skirt are glimpsed in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curvaceous leg' reads as a person; it is a furniture term.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a folding hood.

clue.text: Religious teacher organising a swim

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A guru is arranging a swimming outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu holy man and teacher.

clue.text: Norm hoped letters could be redone in heavy type

indicators.note: redone means the letters of the two words are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: Norm wanted the printing done again in a bold font.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy type' suggests bold print; it is a body type.
explanation.definitionFit: An endomorph is a person with a soft, rounded build, a heavily built body type.

clue.text: Finished game of croquet and collapsed

definitions.meaning: in croquet a player finishes by striking the peg with the ball, so their game is ended
slang for fell down exhausted or died

explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the final peg ends a croquet game, and the same phrase is slang for dropping dead or flaking out.

clue.text: Heathen likely to embrace absolutely nothing

indicators.note: to embrace means the likely word wraps round the nothing

parts.note: prone to means likely to
FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A pagan is liable to accept nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane means irreligious or secular, the outlook of a heathen.

clue.text: Sweet countenance upset by tear

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for face upside down

parts.note: mug is slang for face, countenance
a tear is a drop of liquid from the eye

explanation.surface: A sweet face is upset and spoilt by a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the face; it is a noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumdrop is a chewy jelly confectionery, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Declined to live over the border?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word sits upturned above the next

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a flower bed is a garden border

explanation.surface: Someone refused to live on the far side of the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a frontier; it is a garden flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs as it goes out, so ebbed means faded or declined.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory dye washed out

parts.note: off means gone or removed, as dye washed away
a dye gives colour

explanation.surface: The dye has faded in the wash and the result is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Off colour means slightly unwell or below par, so not satisfactory.

clue.text: The ones indicated — Brown, shortly followed by East

parts.note: Thos is the abbreviation of Thomas, as for Tom Brown of Tom Brown's Schooldays
E is east on the compass

explanation.surface: Here are the ones pointed out: Brown in brief, then East.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative pronoun points out particular things or people.

clue.text: Where directors get together to mount Othello, with backing

parts.note: to mount a ship or horse is to board it

indicators.note: backing signals that the word for Othello is read from end to start

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Theatre directors meet to stage Othello, with financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with backing' looks like money for the production; it turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's board of directors meets in a dedicated room for its meetings.

clue.text: Smooth old comic actor

parts.note: to buff a surface is to polish it smooth

explanation.surface: A slick veteran comedian of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffo is the comic singer in Italian opera, a stock funny performer.

clue.text: Part of skeleton found in Troy

definitions.meaning: the broad upper bone of the pelvis
the Latin name for the ancient city besieged by the Greeks

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the large hip bone and, in Latin, the city of Troy.

clue.text: Adore trips to European city — come down to earth here!

indicators.note: trips suggests stumbling about, so the letters of the first word are jumbled

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone who loves travel takes trips to Rome, landing back on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' reads as journeys, but it scrambles ADORE into AERODR.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is where aircraft land, literally coming down to earth.

clue.text: Lake, you see, reportedly an Irish one -or Swiss

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: reportedly means the next words are taken as heard, as letter names

parts.note: spoken aloud, the two words are the letter names U and C
Lough Erne is a lake in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A lake, you see, is said to be either an Irish one or a Swiss one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' carries 'lake' forward, so 'Swiss' stands for a Swiss lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake of Lucerne lies in central Switzerland, so it is a Swiss lake.

clue.text: Impudence one encountered taking a class with tough exteriors

parts.note: crust is slang for cheek or nerve
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A cheeky ace pupil joins a class of hard-shelled creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is the zoological class of crabs and lobsters, animals with hard shells.

clue.text: Father has to sit for picture holding love child

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: holding means the posing word grips the zero inside it

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A dad has to sit for a portrait while cradling his darling baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A papoose is a Native American baby, or a pouch for carrying an infant, so it means a child.

clue.text: Lay down before Jewish religious authority

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before
the scribes were teachers of Jewish law in the Gospels

explanation.surface: Lie down in front of a rabbi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay down' reads as resting; it means set down a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To prescribe is to lay down rules authoritatively.

clue.text: New text discovered about pirate, a hearty individual

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the pirate
new means the letters of text are made fresh in another order

parts.note: a rover is a sea robber, a pirate

explanation.surface: A newly found document describes a pirate as a jolly fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is a link word; 'New' marks the anagram and 'about' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person is often called hearty.

clue.text: After acclamation for a hit, head of drama is impressed

indicators.note: After places the drama letter behind the fencing call

parts.note: fencers call out touché to acknowledge a hit

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of drama

explanation.surface: Following applause for a smash hit, the drama department's leader is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' suggests a stage success, but it is a fencing touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be touched is to be emotionally moved, as is being impressed.

clue.text: Ran out of water, so used tea-towel

definitions.meaning: became empty, as a well or river does
did the drying of the washed dishes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both ceased to flow and wiped the wet dishes.

clue.text: Entertainer performing overseas?

parts.note: over seas read literally: a seaside show performer works out over the water, on the pier, and the name begins that way

explanation.definitionFit: The white-faced clown of seaside pier shows is a traditional entertainer.

clue.text: Twice fix this sort of camera

parts.note: to pin is to fasten, to fix
a hole is a fix, a tight spot

explanation.surface: Repair this kind of camera two times.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinhole camera has no lens, just a tiny aperture.

clue.text: Boy's punishment inflicted by inn keeper, so to speak?

definitions.text: Boy's punishment inflicted by inn keeper, so to speak?

parts.words: Boy's punishment inflicted by inn keeper, so to speak?
parts.note: a schoolboy kept in after class; an inn keeper read as one who keeps people in

explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in after school is a standard punishment for pupils.

clue.text: Refuse collections here in depression

definitions.meaning: down in the ... means low in spirits

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both rubbish tips and a gloomy mood.

clue.text: Animal caged in many a lab

indicators.note: caged in means the creature is enclosed within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A creature is kept in a cage in many a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about doctor' being in jazz group

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes round the doctor letters

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in surprise at a doctor playing in a jazz band.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small band, typically in jazz or dance music.

clue.text: Joint cover for head of church

definitions.meaning: a corner joint of two angled pieces of wood
the tall headdress of a bishop

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a woodwork corner joint and a bishop's tall hat.

clue.text: Instant tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone at a café is asked whether they want instant tea or coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like the drinks' adjective; it is a noun, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Achieve hardly anything without a ring, as Alfred, for one, discovered

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the phrase goes round the ring

parts.note: to achieve hardly anything is to do little
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Alfred found that he accomplished almost nothing without a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Doolittle is Eliza's father in Shaw's Pygmalion; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred is the dustman father in Shaw's Pygmalion and its musical, bearing this surname.

clue.text: Last pear going off -— little change in other fruit

indicators.note: fruit going off goes bad, so the letters rot into a new order

parts.note: p is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: The last pear in the bowl is going bad, and there is small change for another fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' scrambles LASTPEAR together with P into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The star apple is a tropical fruit, so it is another fruit besides the pear.

clue.text: Rigid monarch needs shock treatment

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A stiff, unbending king needs electric shock therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upright and stiff is rigid.
